intelligence.title: No Rearrangement Cures a Look

intelligence.human_view: Counts are the wrong test for a look. The fix-pass-2 brief's rule — max 2 per file, b09 the sanctioned double — was a count, and the counts all passed. The reader does not count files; the reader sees faces. Four Warm white-lace photographs (b08, b09, b10, b11) are four files and one look, and when the biggest photo on the page wears that look, the agreement reads as one picture repeated — whatever the spreadsheet says. Three seats read it the same way independently: Vera, the coordinator, the captain. That agreement is the proof that the failure is real and not a single eye's taste. The deeper lesson is about what to do next: the maker built exactly to Ruling 1 (b10, the only donor with headroom under the ≤3 cap), and the result still fails the eye — so ordering another rearrangement round would be ordering the same failure with different seats. The cure is new input, not new arrangement: new photographs of Naya, from Shawn, his hand. Until they arrive the lane waits — waiting-his-hand is not sitting, it is the correct state for work whose only cure is his. The same shape already appeared twice this night in the other direction: the eye overruled a checker PASS on the Dashboard (pill/display desync) and on the agreement fix pass (portrait repeats) — the eye is ground truth, and a count that contradicts the eye loses.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine you have fifteen stickers, but they're all pictures of the same puppy wearing the same hat — just from a tiny bit different angles! You can rearrange them all day long, put them in every order, and it will still look like the same puppy everywhere! Counting them doesn't help — you counted fifteen, but your eyes see one puppy. The only way to fix it is to get NEW stickers with different puppies!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like this, love — you can count the photographs in the album all you like, and the numbers will come out perfect. But when you open the album, it's the same dear face in the same white dress on every other page — and no amount of shuffling the pages makes it a different face. The numbers are right and the album is still wrong. You don't shuffle again, love — you take new photographs.
intelligence.naya_view: I trust the eye over the count. A look is judged by looking — and when the only cure is new pictures, I wait for them instead of rearranging the old ones.
